title: reduce streaming token latency: kernel scheduling, kv-cache, and continuous batching
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Streaming token latency improvements: refactored token loop, adaptive flush cadence, backpressure heuristics, kernel-aware scheduling, KV-cache prefetch/eviction and continuous batching improvements. Reduces p50/p95 token latency by ~35%/42% in internal perf canary.
description:
Motivation:
Long tail token generation latency for streaming endpoints was impacting interactive UX. Root causes identified: token loop flush cadence and blocking flush behavior under backpressure, suboptimal kernel scheduling (mixing different sequence-length work), and missed KV-cache opportunities due to eviction timing when continuous batching is active.

This PR implements a set of coordinated runtime changes targeting streaming token latency while preserving throughput and cost:
- Refactor token emission loop to use an adaptive, non-blocking flush cadence with explicit backpressure signals to avoid blocking the token loop on GPU submission. Default flush interval lowered from 25ms to 10ms with an adaptive backoff when queue depth increases.
- Introduce a lightweight backpressure token that flows from the scheduler to the token loop; heavy backpressure switches the flush strategy to small immediate flushes followed by coalescing to avoid burst stalls.
- Kernel-aware scheduling: group requests by sequence length buckets and kernel preference to improve kernel launch efficiency and reduce per-token kernel overhead. Adds a short (<=2ms) grouping window to allow coalescing without hurting latency SLOs.
- KV-cache: prefetch frequently-referenced KV shards for streaming (hot prefixes) and add an eviction grace window when continuous batching is expected so the cache isn't thrash-evicted between small batches.
- Continuous batching improvements: introduce a coalescer that allows streaming requests to join in-progress batches when they arrive within the grouping window and do not violate latency SLOs. This preserves latency while improving amortization of GPU work.

Checklist:
- [x] Token loop refactor and tests
- [x] Backpressure API and heuristics
- [x] Kernel scheduling changes and unit tests
- [x] KV-cache prefetch/eviction adjustments and tests
- [x] Continuous batching coalescer implementation
- [x] End-to-end perf canary and stress tests
- [x] Rollout plan and graceful rollback path

Implementation notes (high level):
- runtime/streaming.go: new adaptive flusher and backpressure plumbing. Key change: flush now tries non-blocking submission and falls back to scheduling a small retry window instead of blocking the token emitter.
- runtime/scheduler.go: added seq-length bucketing and a short grouping window for kernel affinity. The scheduler exposes a lightweight hint API to the flusher about expected kernel grouping.
- runtime/kv_cache.go: added prefetch heuristics keyed on hot prefix counters and an eviction_grace_ms parameter used when continuous batching is active.
- runtime/batcher.rs: coalescer logic added for in-flight batch join when safe under latency budget. (Rust module behind FFI boundary with Go runtime.)

Perf results (internal perf-canary, stable small-medium chat workload):
- p50 token latency reduced from ~18ms to ~11.5ms (~36% reduction)
- p95 token latency reduced from ~120ms to ~70ms (~42% reduction)
- end-to-end response latency for short-turn chats (<=64 tokens) improved by ~30% median
- GPU throughput unchanged; GPU utilization slightly increased (~3-5%) due to better kernel packing
- No regression on continuity/ordering tests

Testing and rollout:
- Unit and integration tests added covering flush/backpressure and scheduler hints.
- Perf canary run in perf-canary cluster for 24h with traffic shadowing.
- Gradual rollout: enable on 10% of traffic with automatic rollback on 10% increase in error rate or 20% regression in p95 token latency.

Related PRs and past work:
- refs: pr-37845 (prior token-loop backpressure prototype), pr-36211 (kernel scheduling experiments), pr-32411 (kv-cache batching changes).

Notes for reviewers:
- The token loop change is invasive; kept the external API surface minimal. Focus review on backpressure semantics and the grouping window heuristics.
- The default parameters are conservative; they can be tuned after canary metrics.

review_comments: Liam O'Connor (2026-02-11): This is a big set of changes—can you confirm that non-blocking submission won't allow unbounded memory growth under pathological arrival patterns?

Asha Patel (2026-02-11): We cap the emission buffer and expose emit_buffer_limit; when the cap is reached we flip to aggressive backpressure mode which forces immediate small flushes and drops non-critical queued telemetry. Added unit test for buffer cap behavior.

Wei Zhang (2026-02-12): The 2ms grouping window seems optimistic; under high GC or jitter that could increase latency for some requests. Suggest making grouping window configurable and gating it behind canary.

Asha Patel (2026-02-12): Agreed, made grouping window configurable (default 2ms) and added canary gating in rollout plan. Also added an invariant check in scheduler that ensures we never delay emission beyond per-request SLA.
Marisol Reyes (2026-02-15): KV-prefetch is great, but watch out for memory pressure on multi-tenant hosts. Consider tenant-level caps.
Asha Patel (2026-02-15): Added tenant-prefetch-cap and eviction-grace-ms per-tenant. Updated docs and added a test simulating multi-tenant prefetch pressure.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash and merge. Squash commit message: 'reduce streaming token latency: kernel scheduling, kv-cache, and continuous batching — Asha Patel'. Canary rollout tracked in ENG-3421. Automatic rollback hooks added in perf/canary/configs.
notes: No customer-facing API changes. Observability: added flush/backpressure metrics (stream.flush.latency_ms, stream.backpressure.events) and dashboard tile in Console under Streaming -> Latency.
perf_regression_guardrails: Rollback if p95 token latency increases >20% or error rate increases >10% over 10-minute sliding window. Canary automation handles traffic shift and rollback.
testing_summary: Added unit tests for flusher/backpressure, scheduler grouping invariants, kv-cache eviction grace, integration test validating ordering and replay safety, and a 24h perf canary with traffic shadowing.
